author: Grace Hall
title: Trump Downplays China Threat to Taiwan - NewsBreak
text:
By Grace Hall ,
41 minutes ago President Donald Trump noted he does not expect China to invade Taiwan and expressed confidence in his relationship with Chinese leader Xi Jinping ahead of their South Korea meeting. Analysts have increasingly warned of increased Chinese military activity and potential long-term threats to Taiwan. Trump stressed U.S. military strength as a deterrent, while experts have noted that increased Chinese incursions in the Taiwan Strait have raised regional concern.
Trump stated, “I think we’ll be just fine with China. China doesn’t want to do that.”
Trump added, “Now that doesn’t mean it’s not the apple of his eye, because probably it is, but I don’t see anything happening.”
A Pentagon assessment reportedly suggested that China may consider attempting to seize Taiwan as early as 2027. Taiwan’s government has urged continued U.S. support.
The United States recognizes only Beijing and is required by law to provide Taiwan with defensive weapons. U.S. policy has remained ambiguous regarding whether Washington would use force to defend the island.
Trump said, “We have the best equipment. We have the best of everything, and nobody’s going to mess with that. And I don’t see that at all with President Xi. I think we’re going to get along very well.”
Trump concluded, “I think when we finish our meetings in South Korea, China and I will have a really fair and really great trade deal together.”
Grace Hall covers U.S. politics & news for content partner Modern Newsstand LLC.
